The framework

What is the Orchard?

The Orchard Cognitive Framework studies the relationships between evidence, context, representation, justified judgment and the authority to use a judgment. Its central concern is how a computational state can change while preserving the obligations that make its decisions accountable.

A change may refine what a system can distinguish, improve how it enquires, or alter the methods available for future repair. Each change needs a declared meaning, scope and qualification boundary.

The laboratory

What have we built?

A modular, deterministic playground for finite Orchard experiments. Every stage has a concrete question, computed results, interventions, boundary probes and clickable plain-English and mathematical definitions.

The first four stages reconstruct selected manuscript mechanisms. Stages five and six are new authored toy studies inspired by the research programme. Browser experiments and standalone Python implementations make their mechanics inspectable.

The possibility

What is MeRSIA?

Meta-recursively self-improving alignment: the proposal that a system could improve its capacity to understand and develop alignment, preserving that developmental path as its computational state changes.

The laboratory demonstrates prerequisites and bounded learning mechanisms. Establishing that alignment development outpaces other capability growth requires a stronger resource model, broader tasks and evidence that remains to be produced.

A glimpse of a much larger body of work

The visible tip.
A much deeper Orchard.

These six experiments are a small window into a framework developed over three decades.

They expose selected mechanics so you can inspect, question and test them. As the author describes it, the vast majority of the Orchard Cognitive Framework—both developed work and work in development—remains below the waterline, outside this demonstration and not yet visible to the wider world.

That broader body of work is an invitation to investigate further. Its undisclosed parts are not additional evidence for the results shown here: this laboratory stands on its visible definitions, calculations and limits.

Inspect the rubric and its evidence

Seven gates are applied to each of six stages. Current evidence supports four gates per stage: a stated contract, a specified mathematical model, finite checks, and matching native-Python numerical results. Independent replication and robustness, measured scale-up, and generalized application are not established. These gates differ greatly in difficulty.

Inspect the complete checklist and supporting references

Python parity is a second implementation check by this project. It is not independent scientific replication. “Finite checks” refers to each declared toy scope, not universal safety or a full MeRSIA proof.

Beyond the first ladder · proposed, not implemented

The next questions are more interesting because the limits are visible.

07

When the obligations change

Can a learned method adapt to new context descriptors or decision obligations while preserving what still has to remain true? Separate genuine transfer from fitting a familiar fixture.

08

When the evidence gets difficult

Test noise, conflicting feedback, missing observations and hostile sources. Invite independent replication and make failures produce inspectable repair tasks.

09+

When the world gets larger

Replace exhaustive enumeration with scalable machinery, measure real resource costs, and seek conditional results that transfer beyond the finite laboratory.

How to run a downloaded experiment

With Python 3.10 or newer installed, run the downloaded file. Its built-in help explains parameters, and it can save a JSON report.

python3 05_bounded_meta_extension.py --help
python3 05_bounded_meta_extension.py --output results.json

The displayed source and download contain the same code. The scripts have no Node.js dependency. Python artifact bindings are local to their implementation; cross-language artifact import is not claimed.

Towards MeRSIA

Six implemented finite experiments

A growing laboratory for learning how to improve alignment. Each milestone needs its own model and evidence; installing a new display does not establish a new capability.

  1. Coupled repairImplementedFixed evidence → qualified rule and view repair → current receiving decision.
  2. Qualified inheritanceImplementedCarry an acquired construction method into an empty child; remove, restore and reconstruct it under matched new evidence.
  3. Constructive enquiryImplementedConstruct questions from action disagreement; compare completion, costs, duties and outside-library errors.
  4. Acquired expressionImplementedUse trusted audited failures to select, validate and retain an expression; remove and restore it in a frozen fresh-dimension census.
  5. Bounded meta-extensibilityImplemented toyAcquire a conservative constructor revision on one task, learn a different repair on another, then test removal, restoration and the remaining depth boundary.
  6. Resource comparisonFirst bounded testCompare fit-only and checked adoption on the same later-learning task. Inspect charged work, frozen response fidelity and faulty-feedback holds. Full relative-rate dominance remains a research target.

Stage one supplies a checked method to stage two. Stage three uses a separately supplied diagnostic compiler and emits an audited failure. Stage four uses that gap to initiate expression acquisition, then tests a frozen library on fresh cases. Stage five replays the acquired model, learns a constructor revision and tests subsequent repair acquisition. Stage six tests a declared resource model under a matched subsequent-learning task. Runtime evidence and receiving grants are new inputs. Live controls stay unchanged.

    Books and different ways into the Orchard

    Foundational mathematics

    THOUGHT — The Science of Recursion

    THOUGHT — The Science of Recursion is an attempt to map the territory of how AI can think safely.

    Read the full description

    It is one of the foundational texts of the Orchard Cognitive Framework. It contains some of the basic machinery taken from nearly thirty years of independent work in cybernetics, information architecture, systems thinking and engineering, and brought into mathematical form through an unusual collaboration between a human researcher and modern AI systems. This book asks what happens when cognition is treated not as a mysterious black box, but as a collection of interacting processes that can be examined, tested and rebuilt. It also asks a question that may matter enormously in the decades ahead:

    If we are going to build minds more powerful than our own, should we not first try to understand the architecture of thought?

    The book also comes with supporting content externally downloadable at no extra cost: Python scripts and exercises to explore if you wish to delve deeper.

    Plain-English companion

    THOUGHTFUL: The Plain English Companion to the Orchard Cognitive Framework

    A thoughtful conversation about artificial intelligence should be open to curious minds from every background. While THOUGHT focuses on the mathematics more formally, THOUGHTFUL opens the discussion up for a much broader range of people.

    Read the full description

    What must a useful memory preserve? When should a system question its answer? How could experience change the way it thinks next time?

    In Thoughtful: A Plain English Guide to the Orchard Cognitive Framework, we explore a developing approach to how artificial intelligence might remember, reason, imagine, act and revise its own methods.

    The journey begins with ordinary experience. A message is misunderstood. A remembered fact has become outdated. A committee reaches a decision without noticing what remains uncertain. From these familiar situations, the book gradually introduces the distinctions and mechanisms behind the Orchard, an ambitious mathematical construct to enable safe AI to be developed, to think safely, to grow closer to humanity rather than further apart.

    Written for interested readers across the humanities, social sciences and technical disciplines, Thoughtful assumes curiosity and careful attention. It introduces the necessary mathematical ideas as they arise, with examples and explanations that give them room to settle. This is the greatest challenge of our time; it affects all of us, and we should all have a chance to understand the technical nuances in plain language.

    Agreement is optional. Understanding should be available for all.

    Small habits of thought

    CRINKLES: Small Rules for Large Minds

    A spell book for an AI generation. Stronger than “vibe coding wisdom for an AI generation.” The “spells” are not promises of supernatural power. They are tiny executable habits of thought.

    Read the full description

    CRINKLES is different from the other works. It makes the subject matter accessible in a bite-size format while sitting on the toilet, waiting for a progress bar, in transit…

    It is not “spell book” in the mystical-claims sense—more like a compact book of symbolic operations, cautions, little transformations, memorable rules, and things you can invoke when your reasoning starts going sideways.

    Open it anywhere and you might get:

    Do not fill the void.

    Or:

    You can know the relationship while not knowing either thing.

    Or just a huge:

    How the methodology developed

    Mathematical Dynamite and Recursive Demolition

    Think Freakonomics for the AI generation—except with more subsea engineering, stranger mathematics, and occasional controlled explosions.

    Read the full description

    For readers interested in some of the most important questions of our day: can we solve AI alignment, what is cognitive architecture, how can we use cybernetics, do we need consciousness studies if AI claims to wake up?

    In Mathematical Dynamite and Recursive Demolition we delve into unorthodox systems engineering, the scientific method dressed in combat gear—or simply the peculiar places a determined mind can end up when it keeps asking… “What happens if we blow up that assumption?”

    This book explores the formation of the methodology that has led to the Orchard Cognitive Framework.

    A laboratory we can extend

    One experiment at a time

    Six modules now share the laboratory. Each has its own reasoning engine, controls, state and checks. Method transfer is qualified within its declared scope; the diagnostic compiler is supplied separately. Current observations and receiving grants are new inputs.

    Possible next encounters

    The next milestone needs comparable resource budgets and separate learning tasks before testing relative development rates. Deeper language growth also needs a new explicit contract and preservation checks.
